channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Altman Says AI Industry ‘Will Be Fine’ After Huang’s Ouster
item.description: OpenAI’s Sam Altman said he believes the artificial intelligence industry will weather the uncertainty prompted by the ousting of Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang last week.
item.dc:creator: Shirin Ghaffary

item.title: Fed's Warsh Says Staff Are Sketching Out AI Contingencies
item.description: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh says staff at the US central bank have begun to sketch out contingencies for how the surging adoption of artificial intelligence might impact the world’s biggest economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Huang’s Ouster Fuels Doubts About Nvidia’s Support for Neoclouds
item.description: Jensen Huang built Nvidia Corp. into the world’s most valuable company and channeled its financial heft into bankrolling neoclouds — a new class of businesses that stockpile chips and rent out computing power.
item.dc:creator: Dawn Lim and Michelle Cheng

item.title: Thoma Bravo’s Proofpoint Launches $2 Billion Debt Deal for M&A
item.description: Thoma Bravo-backed Proofpoint Inc. has kicked off a near $2 billion debt sale to finance an acquisition and extend the maturity of a term loan, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Weinman, Jeannine Amodeo and Gowri Gurumurthy

item.title: Apple Taps 26-Year Veteran Corey Fugman to Run Pay, Card and Wallet Services
item.description: Apple Inc. has tapped a 26-year company veteran as the new head of its payment service and digital wallet unit, a vital part of the iPhone maker’s services business.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: What to Expect From Trump’s China Summit
item.description: Nvidia’s chip exports loom over a high-stakes summit between President Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. Leslie Vinjamuri, the Chicago Council on Global Affairs President & CEO, says she expects few concrete outcomes, but the meeting could reset expectations for diplomacy as Congress weighs tougher export controls and scrutiny of US policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US is Falling Behind on AI Buildout Needs: Midha
item.description: Anthropic founding investor and AMP BPC founder Anjney Midha, joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how the US is struggling to scale compute fast enough to keep pace with China. He also expressed optimism on the leadership of Colette Kress, the Interim CEO of Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia Earnings to Test AI Boom as Hike Looms
item.description: With confidence in the AI buildout key to the economic outlook, Nvidia’s earnings report Tuesday will be the market focus this week alongside October retail data. Jennifer Lee, Senior Economist with BMO Capital Markets, discusses how Wall Street is digesting a mix of economic data and AI-related headlines. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Stocks Sink on Bitcoin's Slide; Aramark Falls on Earnings | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Bitcoin's slide is bringing down crypto stocks including Strategy (MSTR), Coinbase (COIN) and Circle (CRCL) with investors increasingly turning away from the asset class. - Aramark (ARMK) shares are dropping after the food and related products distributor reported adjusted earnings per share and revenue for the fourth quarter that missed the consensus estimates. 2027 guidance includes a slight miss on EPS growth. The midpoint of the organic revenue growth projection is also below the Street estimate. - Blackstone Digital (BXDC) shares are jumping after it agreed to a deal to buy a majority stake in Amazon's data center portfolio. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s CEO Search Draws Fire With Bessent’s Shakeup Call
item.description: Pressure is mounting on Nvidia Corp. days after it ousted Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urging the company to make a “dramatic” leadership shakeup and come clean about its compliance with export controls on its prized AI chips. Ed Ludlow, host of Bloomberg Tech, discusses the Anthropic IPO this week and Nvidia as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urges the company to consider shakeup CEO successor. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google Parent to Take Part in $3 Billion in Prepaid Energy Deals
item.description: Google parent Alphabet Inc. is planning to participate in two upcoming prepaid energy transactions totaling $3 billion.
item.dc:creator: Erin Hudson and Amanda Albright

item.title: Nvidia Backs ‘Genius Grant’ Winner's Push for Cost-Efficient AI
item.description: A five-month-old startup co-founded by two prominent artificial intelligence experts at Stanford University has drawn funding from several large tech firms to help businesses seamlessly improve and customize AI products to suit their needs. Menlo Ventures has led a $110 million round in Noeri, with participation from Madrona Venture Group, Kindred Ventures and NEA. item.dc:creator: Dina Bass

item.title: Odd Lots: The “Trilemma” Behind the US-China AI Arms Race
item.description: On today’s episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Tian Yang, CIO and manager of the VPX fund at Variant Perception, joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to discuss how the Nvidia crisis is revealing the competing pressures facing global powers: keep prices down and consumers happy, while protecting sovereignty. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Is Delaying Some Deals, Moynihan Says
item.description: Bank of America Corp. Chief Executive Officer Brian Moynihan says capital markets activity has been bumpy, and some deals are being delayed until early next year because of the expected Anthropic initial public offering. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Moves to Restrict Remote Access to Advanced AI Chips
item.description: The US Commerce Department issued an interim rule to limit remote access to advanced AI chips and servers from certain countries. The new rule will require licenses to reexport advanced AI chips to Brazil, Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand following increased scrutiny over semiconductor exports after an alleged espionage scandal involving Nvidia Corp. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bank of America CEO Moynihan on IPO Pipeline, AI, Consumer Strength
item.description: Bank of America Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Brian Moynihan says some deals are getting delayed until 2027 because the Anthropic expected blockbuster initial public offering is crowding out smaller companies. He also talks about using AI, earnings and his own succession plans. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CATL, Baidu, Unitree to Attend APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen
item.description: Top executives from some of China’s biggest companies are converging in Shenzhen, the southern Chinese technology hub, for a week of high-stakes diplomacy and deal-making that will also bring US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin to the city.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: JPM’s Michele: ‘Looks a Bit Silly’ Fed Missed Oct. Hike
item.description: Bob Michele, global head of fixed income at JPMorgan Asset Management, sees the Federal Reserve having a bigger impact on the Treasury market at the moment than the AI trade. Michele says “it’s looking a little bit silly” that the Fed missed a chance to hike rates in October. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Revolut Ordered to Improve Money Laundering Controls in Italy
item.description: Revolut’s Italy unit was found to have weaknesses in its anti-money laundering controls by a Milan court, which said the digital bank negligently facilitated criminal activity placing it under supervision for one year.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Lepido, Antonio Vanuzzo and Alberto Brambilla

item.title: Baidu Posts Sixth Straight Sales Drop After AI Drag Persists
item.description: Baidu Inc. posted its sixth straight quarterly revenue drop, underscoring the urgency of its efforts to commercialize AI to offset a faltering legacy search business.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
